prose: Richard Ng argues that OpenAI's new ChatGPT Space, a shared document space where people tag in ChatGPT or Codex, could become a context-centralisation flywheel giving one company dystopian power over how organisations learn and build IP. He sees real product and commercial promise, citing Microsoft 365's roughly $100bn revenue, but his essay is a polemic against any one firm owning everyone's context, followed by a two-minute open-source proof of concept as an alternative. Basis: the first part of a long essay was read.
highlights: ChatGPT Space: shared living documents with ChatGPT and Codex.
Fear: one firm absorbing and commoditising organisations' expertise.
Offers an open-source proof of concept instead.
Basis: first part of the essay.
